title: Muscle symptoms
summary: Muscle pain, cramps or weakness. Overexertion is considered if the context supports it. Severe muscle pain, weakness, or tea- or cola-colored urine reported after exertion or heat requires ruling out rhabdomyolysis. A muscle measurement with a pending method or an isolated RGB value never triggers that hypothesis. Sudden focal weakness is handled by the neurological route. Design decision: suspected rhabdomyolysis uses review_required urgency with the action 'immediate medical assessment', because the source calls for assessment rather than an onboard emergency alert. Informational support only: not a diagnosis or a treatment decision. There are no clinical personnel on board: the steps are first aid and monitoring; treatment depends on mission procedures.

suspected_rhabdo.text: The pattern requires ruling out rhabdomyolysis: stop exertion and do not ignore the signs.
notify: mission control (if the link is up)

steps.text: Note the urine color and when the symptoms started; they can appear hours or days after exertion.

missing_guidance: Confirming it requires a blood creatine kinase (CK) test, which the assistant does not have; treatment depends on the mission procedure (not loaded).

review.text: Muscle pain or cramps: local care and monitoring. If dark urine or weakness appears, the situation changes.
notify: mission control (if the link is up)

steps.text: Gently stretch or massage the muscle.
Apply heat if the muscle is tight and cold if it is sore.
Drink more fluids if you may be dehydrated.
If tea- or cola-colored urine or weakness appears, report it: it requires ruling out rhabdomyolysis.

candidates.label: Overexertion
candidates.minimum_evidence: Muscle pain or cramps after reported exertion.

candidates.label: Rhabdomyolysis (must be ruled out)
candidates.minimum_evidence: After exertion or heat: reported severe muscle pain, weakness, or tea- or cola-colored urine.
